frequency_question: How often do administrations successfully finalize high-magnitude contested regulatory fee hikes when they set out to do so within a multi-year window?
membership_rule: Includes major agency actions proposing unprecedented fee escalations or penalty spikes in immigration, environmental, or financial domains where the administration explicitly championed the initiative. Excludes routine inflationary adjustments.

cases.name: Reagan Administration fee-for-service structural cost recovery overhaul
Clinton Administration INS user fee restructuring
Bush II Administration SEC registration fee increases
Obama Administration USCIS premium processing and immigration fee schedule major revision
Trump I Administration USCIS fee rule (attempted major hike)
Biden Administration fee for certain employment-based petitions and USCIS comprehensive fee rule

provenance_note: rate of 100% from only 6 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 6 named major administrative fee rule revisions over 40 years representing top-tier executive intent.
known_gaps: Does not account for rules abandoned internally before formal publication, though these are rare when principals signal high priority.
validity_reason: Spans the current presidential term; executive authority over agency rulemaking structures remains consistent under the APA.
